studyScope: Historical 2023 proposal and 2024 Phase 3 response document; no assertion about currently operative regulations.
selection: Section 2.5 was selected after reviewing its responses and the earlier two-request pilot. All seven organization blocks within this finite section were then read. This is a retrospective inventory of agency-selected excerpts, not a prospective sample or a docket/comment denominator.
sourceAuthentication: Visual review of all six section pages and two Appendix A pages in the official downloaded PDF, whose SHA-256 matches the prior pilot. Source projections and CSV fingerprints allow offline consistency checks; they do not independently authenticate the PDF or validate manual segmentation and coding.

responseDocument.boundaryReview: Section 2.5 starts partway down PDF 457 after the end of section 2.4, which is excluded. The section's response ends on PDF 462. Text extraction places section 2.6 on the following page; that next section was not coded.
responseDocument.responseScope: One section-level summary and response contains a collective method discussion and three separately named responses. Named mention in the summary is not individual causal attribution. For unresolved requests, response page fields identify the searched section response, not a matched disposition. An absent request-specific disposition here is not an unanswered comment across the docket.

codebook.segmentation: Retain each separable requested action or explanation. Split Volvo's joint call to reconsider standard-setting and vehicle categorization into two actions. Split China's method/source question from international comparability. Preserve PACCAR's conditional implementation-date fallback as a separate request with its parent recorded.
codebook.deduplication: Repeated statements by the same organization about the same requested action within this section are one request. DTNA's engineering-judgment request on original page 76 and in response to EPA request 53 is one request, not multiple observations. Repetition elsewhere in the document has not been deduplicated.
codebook.exclusions: Do not treat EPA's quoted requests for comment as industry requests. DTNA's response to EPA request 54 refers elsewhere without a new substantive request in the excerpt; response 55 repeats the reference to response 53. Neither creates an additional request. Explanatory examples, numerical illustrations and expressions of support are context, not extra requests.

responseLinkCodes.explicit_named_response: The response expressly names the organization and addresses this request.
responseLinkCodes.named_summary_collective_response: The summary identifies the organization's concern and a shared response addresses the requested policy direction; no individual effect is inferred.
responseLinkCodes.section_resolution_only: The described section-level resolution can be compared with the request, without an expressly named response or summary link.
responseLinkCodes.no_request_specific_disposition: No separate disposition of this requested action is identified within the reviewed section; this does not establish absence elsewhere.

dispositionCodes.disagreed_with_error_claim: EPA expressly rejects the alleged NPRM calculation error.
dispositionCodes.clarified_existing_scope: EPA clarifies that existing eligibility continues, not that new eligibility was granted.
dispositionCodes.explained_comparability_limit: EPA explains why numerical international comparisons depend on testing assumptions; it does not provide a numerical reconciliation.
dispositionCodes.consistent_with_collective_revision: The direction of the request is consistent with the shared described revision; this is not full acceptance or individual attribution.
dispositionCodes.inconsistent_with_described_resolution: The requested direction conflicts with the described resolution, without an explicit named rejection.
dispositionCodes.no_request_specific_disposition: The section does not separately resolve the precise requested action or explanation.
dispositionCodes.conditional_fallback_not_separately_reso: The requested delay was conditional on adopting a proposal that EPA says it did not finalize; no separate adoption of the requested date is shown.

organizationBlocks.organization: China WTO/TBT National Notification & Enquiry Center

requests.requestSummary: Correct the alleged errors in five of six proposed LHD vocational standard calculations before finalization.
requests.codingRationale: The response expressly disagrees that the NPRM contained the alleged error and says the commenter misunderstood the method. A separate collective method revision is not acceptance of this allegation.

requests.requestSummary: Specify that vehicles without an installed propulsion engine use CI Multi-Purpose standards, rather than urban or regional standards.
requests.codingRationale: CARB appears in the reproduced blocks but is not named in the section summary. The shared response retains CI certification while permitting appropriate urban, regional or multi-purpose categorization, contrary to the requested Multi-Purpose-only limitation. This is not coded as an explicit rejection of CARB.

requests.requestSummary: Clarify the calculation method and sources of the proposed 2027-2032 vocational CO2 standard values in Table II-19.
requests.codingRationale: The named response explains international comparability limits but does not reconstruct the requested proposed table or identify its input sources. The shared discussion describes a revised final method and points to the RIA; it is not treated as a verified complete answer to this distinct proposed-table question.

requests.requestSummary: Explain whether differences between the proposed calculated standards and cited international methods or values are reasonable.
requests.codingRationale: EPA names China WTO and explains that payload, test weight, aerodynamic assumptions and drive cycles affect numerical CO2 values. This is a qualitative comparability explanation, not a numerical reconciliation or endorsement of the comment's international-standard premise.

requests.requestSummary: Clarify that the CO2 credit equation applies to tractors as well as vocational vehicles.
requests.codingRationale: EPA names Cummins and confirms continued tractor credit eligibility. The proposed vocational reference was not intended to exclude tractors; this is clarification rather than newly granted eligibility.

requests.requestSummary: Allow manufacturers to use engineering judgment to choose an appropriate ZEV regulatory subcategory based on the vehicle replaced.
requests.codingRationale: EPA names DTNA's engineering-judgment request in its summary and describes retaining appropriate urban, regional or multi-purpose certification. Repeated request wording and cross-references within this block are collapsed. Agreement in direction is not an individual effect or proof that every requested flexibility was adopted.

requests.requestSummary: Exempt ZEV-generated ABT credits from the averaging-set limitations in 40 CFR 1037.740.
requests.codingRationale: The excerpt contains this distinct request in DTNA's answer to EPA request 53. Section 2.5's response does not separately resolve the averaging-set exemption. Other response sections and the original letter's referenced sections were not reviewed for this request.

requests.requestSummary: Continue allowing ZEV credit calculation in any appropriate vocational subcategory according to intended use instead of requiring Multi-Purpose categorization.
requests.codingRationale: EPA names PACCAR's intended-use and lead-time concerns in its summary and describes not finalizing the common-reference approach. This is shared policy-direction consistency, not an individually identified effect.

requests.requestSummary: If EPA nevertheless requires Multi-Purpose categorization, defer implementation until at least MY2030.
requests.codingRationale: EPA summarizes the requested delay but says it is not finalizing the common-reference approach that triggers this fallback. The section does not separately adopt MY2030. The fallback must not be counted as an unconditional delay request or a second successful reform change.

requests.requestSummary: Re-evaluate the vocational stringency-setting procedure because common absolute reductions have different consequences across manufacturers' vehicle mixes.
requests.codingRationale: EPA summarizes Volvo's standard-setting concern and describes changing to a tractor-like method after considering comments. The request and shared revision align in direction, without establishing that Volvo caused the revision or validating the numerical examples in the excerpt.

requests.requestSummary: Re-evaluate the proposed requirement to categorize zero-emission vocational vehicles in CI Multi-Purpose service classes.
requests.codingRationale: The second part of Volvo's joint request concerns categorization rather than the standard-setting calculation. EPA's shared response permits the appropriate subcategory. These two Volvo requests are not independent comments or independently attributable policy changes.

appendixSelectionContext.scope: Appendix A introduction, Tables A-1/A-2 and general response only; Table A-3's individual comment list and original submissions were not reviewed.
appendixSelectionContext.interpretation: EPA says these general/non-specific comments do not require detailed responses beyond responses elsewhere in the document. Not reproduced does not mean not received or unanswered. The eight theme counts sum to incidences across comments, not unique comments; the appendix cannot be added to this section as a control or nonresponse denominator.
appendixSelectionContext.sourcePercentageCaveat: The preceding prose gives environmental justice as 28.0 percent while Table A-2 gives 28.1 percent. Counts are retained; no source percentage is silently corrected or used as a comment-level response rate.

remainingReview: Independently review the seven-block inventory, eleven-request segmentation, opposing CARB position, grouped response links and conditional fallback. Obtain and version-match original submissions. Search other response sections for unresolved requests only as a separate declared extension. Before docket rates, define and acquire an independent comment population and a rule for repeated/grouped responses. No causal comparison or simulator recalibration is cleared.
